data.about: The Lufthansa hangar truss carries two vertical roof loads and one inclined load whose direction can be swung on an arc. A trial funicular through an arbitrary pole finds the line of action of the resultant; since support A is a vertical roller, the three-force rule closes the load line and splits the pin reaction at B into B_V and B_H. The force diagram then grows joint by joint. At the default loads the resultant happens to pass through B: A_V = 0, and members 10 and 11 carry nothing — swing the inclined load and they wake up.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the rectangle A–B–D–C with top chord C–E–D and the inner nodes F, G — circles of the same radius around C, E and D place them (the ChangeGeometryofTruss slider spreads the triangle); eleven members, numbered
steps.title: The hangar truss

steps.caption: left: F₁ at C and F₂ at E act vertically; F₃ at D is INCLINED — its direction is the line through H, which rides on an arc around D (drag H!) — right: F₁, F₂, F₃ stacked tip-to-tail: O → P → Q → S, F₃ parallel to H–D
steps.title: Three loads

steps.caption: right: the dashed line O → S closes the load line: the resultant of all three loads — but where does it act? (left: unknown yet)
steps.title: The resultant R₁₂₃

steps.caption: right: any trial pole T with rays to O, P, Q, S — left: from U on the wall line, one string per load, each parallel to its ray
steps.title: A trial funicular

steps.caption: left: the outer strings, extended, meet at Z — R₁₂₃ acts on the line through Z parallel to O–S (dashed green, with the arrow)
steps.title: The line of action

steps.caption: left: support A is a vertical roller — its line meets R₁₂₃’s line of action at S₃, so the pin reaction at B must point along S₃–B (dashed) — right: from O vertically, from S parallel to S₃–B: they close the load line at C₁
steps.title: The three-force rule

steps.caption: right: A_V = C₁ → O, then B’s reaction S → C₁ splits into B_V (drawn beside the load line) and B_H — left: the supports push back (green symbols at A and B)
steps.title: The reactions

steps.caption: left: at C only F₁, member 1 and member 2 meet — right: from P parallel to 2, from O parallel to 1 → G₁ closes the joint
steps.title: Joint C — members 1 and 2

steps.caption: right: from O parallel to member 10 and horizontally for member 11: with A_V ≈ 0 the polygon collapses — the applet’s orange verdict: 10 = 0, 11 = 0, A_V = 0 (swing F₃ or drag H and they wake up!)
steps.title: Joint A — nothing to carry

steps.caption: left: at B the reactions B_V, B_H meet members 8, 9 (and the empty 11) — right: from H₁ parallel to 9, from S parallel to 8 → I₁
steps.title: Joint B — members 8 and 9

steps.caption: left: at F members 1, 9, 10 are known; 3 and 4 close it — right: from G₁ parallel to 3, from I₁ parallel to 4 → J₁
steps.title: Joint F — members 3 and 4

steps.caption: left: at E the load F₂ meets members 2, 3, 5, 6 — right: from Q parallel to 6, from J₁ parallel to 5 → K₁
steps.title: Joint E — members 5 and 6

steps.caption: left: at D the inclined F₃ meets members 6 and 7 — right: K₁ → S is parallel to member 7: the last joint closes exactly on S (the check at G is automatic)
steps.title: Joint D closes — member 7

steps.caption: right: O → S re-appears — loads, reactions and all eleven member forces circulate in one closed diagram — left: the line of action still passes through the same Z
steps.title: The check: R₁₂₃ again

steps.caption: members resolve blue = compression (the fan 1, 3, 5, 7 and the long diagonals) and pink = tension (top chord pieces 2, 6, the tie 4, the deck 11) — pipes ∝ force; drag H, A, O, T, the sliders — click a joint for its equilibrium
steps.title: Compression and tension
